## The question

**Is educational attainment associated with leaning Democratic rather than Republican, after accounting for age and household income?**

Our intended audience is U.S. citizens aged 18 and older who are interested in politics. This question matters because it helps us understand whether differences in political leaning across education levels persist after accounting for age and income.

We use the [2024 American National Election Studies (ANES) Time Series Study](https://electionstudies.org/data-center/2024-time-series-study/), May 19, 2026 release. The dataset contains 5,521 respondents and 1,738 variables, with one row per respondent. ANES combines newly recruited address-based samples with returning panel participants and collects interviews through online, in-person, telephone, and paper surveys. Our analysis uses pre-election variables.

The response is binary political leaning, constructed from party identification (`V241227x`): Democratic identifiers and Democratic-leaning independents (categories 1–3) are coded 1, while Republican identifiers and Republican-leaning independents (categories 5–7) are coded 0. Neutral independents and missing or invalid responses are excluded. The main predictor is education (`V241465x`), with age (`V241458x`) and household income (`V241567x`) included as additional predictors. Education and income are treated as categorical variables. Our proposal's data checks identified 4,640 complete observations for this analysis.

ANES permits research and statistical use with citation and protection of respondent privacy. We will report aggregate results. Limitations include self-reported responses, potential selection bias from missing data, income measured in brackets, and ages capped at 80. Population-level conclusions require appropriate survey weights and consideration of the sampling design. This observational study can identify associations but cannot establish causation.

## What the baseline shows

Our baseline is multiple logistic regression with Democratic versus Republican leaning as the binary response and education, age, and household income as predictors. Logistic regression is appropriate because the response has two categories.
